text:
Predicates:
Employees(x) ::: x is an employee.
SchedulesMeeting(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
InCompanyToday(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
Lunchtime(x, y) ::: x has lunch in y.
AtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
WorkingRemotely(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
EmployeeInOtherCountry(x) ::: x is an employee in another country.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
James ::: the individual James.

Premises:
∀x (SchedulesMeeting(x, y) ∧ Employee(y) → InCompanyToday(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers appear in the company today.
∀x (Lunchtime(x, y) ∧ y = inCompany) → SchedulesMeeting(x, y) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (Lunchtime(x, y)) → (y = inCompany ∨ y = atHome) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or at home.
AtHome(x) → WorkingRemotely(x) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (EmployeeInOtherCountry(x)) → WorkingRemotely(x) ::: All employees in other countries work remotely from home.
¬∃x (Manager(x) ∧ WorkingRemotely(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
James ∧ Manager(James) ∨ (¬Manager(James) ∧ ¬InCompanyToday(James)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today, or neither is true.
